content: This medication can cause a severe intestinal condition known as Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea, which is caused by the bacterium C. difficile. This condition may develop during treatment or even weeks to months after the treatment has been discontinued. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Similarly, in Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to ceftazidime or avibactam, or to penicillins, beta-lactam antibiotics, other cephalosporins, or beta-lactamase inhibitors (e.g., sulbactam). Additionally, disclose any other allergies you may have. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Ceftazidime/avibactam may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if clearly necessary. Ceftazidime is known to pass into breast milk, but it is unclear whether avibactam does as well. Drug interactions may alter the way your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as Coombs' tests or urine glucose tests, potentially causing false results. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition. Laboratory and/or medical tests, such as kidney function tests, should be conducted while you are using this medication. Ensure you attend all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. It is important to take each dose as scheduled. For storage, refer to the product instructions and consult your pharmacist for specific details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
